item.description:
Flow 3.11.0

More download sorting options

Sort by file name, file type, date added, size, progress, speed, time remaining, status, priority or storage location, alongside queue order. The compact arrow button switches ascending/descending order. Flow remembers both selections between launches.

File names sort naturally (File 2 before File 10), using the readable titles shown in the list. Unknown sizes/speeds/time estimates stay at the bottom in either direction. Equal values retain queue order. Sorting changes the displayed list without changing download priority or queue scheduling.

Flow 3.10.1

Reliable Keychain ownership

The native bridge now hands login headers to Flow itself through a local memory pipe. The app owns and reads its own Keychain records, avoiding access stalls between different executables. No login headers enter arguments, inbox files or history.

Optional browser-login downloads

In the browser extension, paste an HTTPS file link and select “Use browser login for this link”. The browser asks for access to that site. Flow stores only matching session headers in macOS Keychain, never in download history. Headers are stripped on redirects to other origins. Automatic capture continues to use public links.

Authenticated downloads retain their saved bytes if login becomes unavailable. Use “Use next Chrome link” when refreshing an expired authenticated download, then send a fresh link with browser login enabled. Forget login through download actions or Properties. Saved login is deleted when a download completes or is removed.

Chrome/Edge extension 2.4.0 is required for the new option; reload an existing unpacked extension after updating its files.
